subtype: Building a kinder relationship with the body [Response]
passage:
Ganga: how's the new plan going?
Ramesh: Day 40. Muted about thirty fitness accounts that made me feel like trash.
Ramesh: My feed is now mostly cooking videos and street dogs.
Ganga: honestly an upgrade
Ramesh: Also breakfast, lunch and dinner at the same times. My alarm says "fuel, not punishment".
Ganga: that is so you. And how's your head about it?
Ramesh: Mixed. Yesterday I carried Nani's gas cylinder up three floors and thought, huh, these legs did that. First nice thing I've said about them in years.
Ganga: that's huge.
Ramesh: Some days are still bad though. Like, really bad.
Ganga: are you still seeing the counsellor at the clinic?
Ramesh: Every Tuesday. She says the bad days are exactly why I keep going.
Ganga: proud of you. Samosa on Friday? Just for fun, no commentary.
Ramesh: deal

qa.q: How did Ramesh feel after carrying Nani's gas cylinder up three floors?
qa.a: Ramesh felt surprised and a little proud, appreciating what those legs could do.

qa.q: Which choice shows Ramesh taking the bad days seriously?
qa.a: Ramesh keeps seeing the counsellor at the clinic every Tuesday instead of stopping once things improved.

qa.q: What is Ganga offering with the Friday samosa plan?
qa.a: Ganga offers ordinary company and food without any remarks about bodies, backing up Ramesh's kinder habits.

grounding: It shows a young adult valuing what the body can do, muting harsh accounts, eating regular meals, speaking kindly of themselves and staying with a counsellor.

passage: The bus to the district town rattled past mustard fields, and Alka's cousin Rekha held up her phone. "Selfie? Wait, let me put the slimming filter." Alka covered the screen, laughing. "No filter. My face came all this way, it can be in the photo." A year ago Alka would have deleted every picture of herself. She had skipped meals, checked her reflection in every shop window and called herself ugly under her breath. When it got bad enough that she fainted at the tailoring shop, her mother took her to the doctor, and now she saw a counsellor in town every other Saturday. That was where they were going. At the bus stand Alka bought two plates of poha. "Lunch first. Always lunch first." Rekha frowned at her own face in the bus window. "I look huge today." "You look like someone who climbed to the hilltop temple faster than me this morning," Alka said.

qa.q: What did Alka buy at the bus stand?
What does Alka's laughing "No filter" suggest about how she now feels about her face?
qa.a: It suggests she feels comfortable being seen as she is, unlike a year ago when she deleted every picture of herself.

qa.q: What turning point led Alka to a counsellor?
qa.a: When she fainted at the tailoring shop, her mother took her to the doctor, which led to regular counselling in town.

qa.q: How might Rekha feel hearing Alka's reply about the hilltop temple?
qa.a: Rekha may feel surprised and a little lighter, hearing her body praised for what it did instead of judged for how it looks.

grounding: It shows a young woman in a small town refusing filters, eating regular meals, speaking kindly about bodies and keeping up counselling after a serious struggle.
